bug_semantics: find-my-way lookup() forwards unsanitized req.method into find(), which does currentNode = this.trees[method] on a prototype-bearing object (this.trees = {}). Inherited keys such as constructor, toString, and __proto__ therefore resolve to Object.prototype properties instead of undefined. The truthy/undefined checks do not reject those values, so find() treats Function or Object.prototype as a radix node and throws when reading currentNode.prefix.length (originally split as prefix = currentNode.prefix; prefixLen = prefix.length). HTTP/2 is the remote trigger because Node's HTTP/2 :method is not restricted to http.METHODS the way HTTP/1 is. Route registration (on/off) does assert http.METHODS, but the request path never did.

The sink is prototype-chain lookup of an untrusted HTTP method on this.trees, then using the result as a router node until prefix.length throws. That map did not exist on 57e7a6d/ce6d38b, which kept one Node in this.tree and only used method as a handlers[] key after a real node was already in hand. PR #168 introduced one tree per method stored in a plain object. Intermediate force-pushes that briefly used a MethodMap constructor are not surviving objects; even that design would still inherit Object.prototype, so the surviving {} assignment is the first-write of the shipped mechanism. Later find() refactors (node-class rewrite, findRoute, GET fast-path) still index this.trees[method] and are not BICs. The 2026 fork-merge fix is the first Object.create(null) on this.trees and is the direct patch; it is in v9.7.0 and not in v9.6.0.
